title: Worksheet 4: String Concatenation
directions: Read the paragraph below carefully. Then answer all questions using ONLY the information in the paragraph. Circle the letter of the best answer.
paragraph: String concatenation is the process of joining two or more strings together to form a single, longer string. In many programming languages, concatenation is performed using the plus symbol (+), similar to how addition works with numbers, but when used with strings, the plus symbol joins the text together end to end instead of adding numeric values. For example, concatenating the string "Hello, " with the string "world!" produces the single combined string "Hello, world!" Programmers often use concatenation to build custom messages that include changing information, such as combining the fixed text "Your score is " with a variable that stores a player's current score, so the final message displayed changes depending on the player's actual score. One common mistake when concatenating is forgetting to include a space between two pieces of text, which can accidentally cause two words to run together, such as producing "Helloworld!" instead of the intended "Hello world!"
